Having edit capabilities universally always would probably lead to abuse of it e.g. changing a title to "Hitler did nothing wrong" after it gets popular. However, allowing mods an option to toggle it would definitely be a convenient change.
Add an option in each subverse to allow editing of titles and/or comments

Also cool would be some sort of ticket system. For instance:

You make a title called "Ctue bunny nuzzles a kit ten" and see that you've made some serious typos. You click the "edit" button and a text entry form pops up asking what you want to change the title to. You type in "Cute bunny nuzzles a kitten!" and press Save. Now your proposed edit is sent to a queue for the moderators to look at. They can either approve or deny it. There is an optional box to send a short custom message to the user if the mod wants to deny the edit. (A denial sends a generic notification otherwise.) The moderator approves it, and the title is changed.

OR

You type in the title "DAE agree we should make cops wear cameras?", wait awhile, and then click edit. In the box, you type "DAE think Hitler was a pretty cool guy?" and hit Save. The mods see this, hit deny, and add a custom message saying "If you try this again you get a ban."

Basically, it's moderator approval for edits just like for posting.

Edit, haha: I don't think comment edits are a big enough deal to need mod approval but it could be an option. To my knowledge Reddit and most forum sites I've seen haven't had any formalized way to edit titles. It typically seems to be a matter of messaging a mod. It would be nice to have that process automated a bit to cut down on the "Oops, typo in title. Can a mod change this?" posts I saw sometimes on Reddit.

Why don't we give a short time (~2mins) to change the title of the submission? This way, moderators don't have to get involved, and it won't be able to abuse the system by changing the title after it gets popular?

I agree with this for posts. Post typos are almost always noticed (in my experience) right after you post it. Comment typos sometime go for longer until you're, for whatever reason, rereading your comment a bit later, so comment edits should be allowed later as well.
